rule: Performance-related implementation may not begin until its unit is active, its parent stage is current, and a reproducible budget/test profile is defined where runtime performance is applicable.

units.name: Performance Measurement & Attribution Foundation
units.summary: Provider-neutral frontend/RUM/backend profiling primitives with Admin/server traces, Theme/Extension attribution, budgets and regression baselines.

architecture.boundary_notes: Instrumentation must be provider-neutral and may not give profilers or packages privileged access around Nexora contracts/capabilities.

data.persistence_impact: Performance profiles, baselines, aggregates, traces/findings and package attribution require bounded/versioned storage with retention policy.
data.migration_policy: Additive portable migrations only; raw trace storage may use adapter-backed external storage later.
data.rollback_notes: Instrumentation can be disabled independently; schema rollback must not require destructive down migrations.

authorization.tenant_impact: All stored tests/RUM/budgets/traces are site/tenant scoped; cross-tenant comparison is denied by default.

security.security_notes: Deep profiling can expose sensitive request/SQL/runtime context. Redaction, sampling, access controls, bounded overhead and no-secret capture are mandatory.

privacy.consent_impact: RUM collection must integrate with PRIVACY-CONSENT-100 and respect applicable GPC/DNT/consent policy.
privacy.retention_impact: Raw traces and RUM identifiers require short configurable retention and privacy-safe aggregation.

units.rollback: Profiling features and RUM intake can be disabled without disabling site rendering; bad instrumentation must fail open for availability but fail closed for claims/evidence integrity.
acceptance_criteria: Frontend, Admin and backend requests can be measured with a canonical provider-neutral result model.
Theme/Extension/App execution and owned assets can be attributed without double-counting nested cost.
Versioned performance budgets and baseline comparisons can detect intentional frontend/backend/package regressions.
Sensitive trace/RUM data is redacted, scoped and retained according to policy.
out_of_scope: Final production Core Web Vitals certification

units.name: Code Quality Intelligence
units.summary: Core/Theme/Extension/App static and build quality analysis correlated with runtime performance evidence while remaining separate from Sentinel security trust.

architecture.boundary_notes: Security findings remain owned by security/Sentinel; quality findings may warn/block only according to explicit quality policy.

data.persistence_impact: Versioned findings, analyzer identity, source/build identity and package profiles.
data.migration_policy: Additive portable metadata tables; large analyzer artifacts remain externalizable.
data.rollback_notes: Analyzer providers can be disabled/replaced without mutating package source.

authorization.tenant_impact: Site/package quality results follow site/package visibility and publisher permissions.

security.security_notes: Analyzers process untrusted package source and build artifacts; analysis must not execute uploaded code outside the existing trust/isolation policy.

privacy.consent_impact: No RUM dependency for static quality findings.

units.rollback: Quality policies and analyzers are versioned; disabling a provider does not rewrite source history or security trust state.
acceptance_criteria: Core and supported package source/builds produce reproducible quality findings with analyzer/version identity.
Quality results cover static/type/lint/complexity/duplication/dead-code/bundle dimensions where applicable.
Runtime performance evidence can link back to responsible source/package where attribution is available.
Quality verdicts remain distinct from Sentinel security decisions.

units.name: Nexora Performance Intelligence Center
units.summary: PageSpeed/GTmetrix-class performance analysis and monitoring with field/lab data, waterfall, filmstrip/video, scripted profiles, frontend/backend/package attribution, history/alerts and AI-grounded recommendations.

architecture.boundary_notes: External browser runners are isolated workers. Provider-specific Lighthouse/CrUX/etc. data is normalized into Nexora result contracts.

data.persistence_impact: Tests, profiles, reports, waterfalls, attachments, trends, alert state and comparison metadata.
data.migration_policy: Metadata is relational/portable; large traces/video/filmstrips use storage adapters.
data.rollback_notes: Historical evidence remains readable when providers change; report schema versions are preserved.

authorization.tenant_impact: Reports/monitors/alerts are tenant/site scoped; external tests require explicit permission and rate limits.

security.security_notes: Arbitrary URL/browser testing creates SSRF/open-proxy/browser-escape risk. Private/reserved networks, metadata endpoints, redirect rebinding and access to platform secrets/internal services must be prevented by isolated runners and egress policy.

privacy.consent_impact: Field/RUM views inherit PRIVACY-CONSENT-100; authenticated scripted flows require explicit operator configuration and secret-safe runner handling.
privacy.retention_impact: Video, traces and RUM aggregates have configurable retention/redaction.

evidence: AI explanation grounded in report evidence

units.rollback: Monitoring/runners/AI recommendations are independently disableable; report history and budget evidence remain immutable/auditable; release-budget override requires permission/reason/audit.
acceptance_criteria: Users can run reproducible mobile/desktop performance tests and inspect field/lab metrics, waterfall and frontend/backend/package evidence.
Reports can compare releases/branches/Theme or Extension versions and identify the responsible measured cost.
External URL testing is isolated and cannot reach private/internal networks or act as an open proxy.
AI recommendations cite report evidence and cannot fabricate a performance PASS.
